Safe source lifecycle
  1. Keep the title and source in owner-private local files.
  2. Run ./pixel work-knowledge-guide add from the trusted terminal with the exact local vault, source, owner, classification, and retention options.
  3. Inspect the plain-language review, then type its short exact APPLY phrase. Any source or vault drift cancels the confirmation.
  4. Use setup, find, remove, rotate, or reconcile for the other guided operations. Rotation and historical reconciliation additionally require the controller to be offline.
Local and explicit. This page never receives source text, titles, file paths, vault keys, or deletion authority. It cannot retrieve, ingest, delete, rotate, or restore knowledge. The plain-language trusted-terminal guide keeps those sensitive operations outside the browser while preserving exact review and confirmation.

Trusted terminal recovery sequence
  1. Validate the exact backup: ./pixel restore /ABSOLUTE/BACKUP.tar.gz.age --identity /OFFLINE/AGE-IDENTITY --validate-only
  2. Rehearse into a new empty root: ./pixel restore /ABSOLUTE/BACKUP.tar.gz.age --identity /OFFLINE/AGE-IDENTITY --rehearse /NEW/EMPTY/ROOT
  3. Review the isolated result and automatic safety-backup destination before an exact --replace --confirm restore.
  4. For containment, follow INCIDENT-RESPONSE.md, inspect broker authority state, and resume only with ./pixel ops-resume "reviewed reason" --confirm or ./pixel frontier-resume "reviewed reason" --confirm.
Terminal-only safety boundary. This page never reads a backup, decryption identity, private incident evidence, or current broker pause state. It cannot rehearse, restore, recover, or resume anything. A recorded successful pause is only a reason to inspect terminal state—not proof that authority is still paused.
